result:
Done. Typecheck passes, `bun test` is 4/4 green, and `guren check` now reports `routes/admin.ts wiring: routes/admin.ts's registrar is called from routes/web.ts` (previously the one failure).

The endpoint's code was all present — `routes/admin.ts` exported a `registerAdminRoutes(router)` registrar that mounts `GET /admin/posts` → `AdminPostController.index` behind the `auth` alias, and `AdminPostController` already built the `{ data: [...] }` payload with authors eager-loaded and `orderBy('id', 'desc')` — but nothing ever called that registrar, so the route was never registered and Hono fell through to a 404 for guests and signed-in users alike. I fixed it in `routes/web.ts` by importing `registerAdminRoutes` from `./admin.js` and calling it with `router` right after `registerAuthRoutes(router)`, which is where the router already carries the `auth`/`guest` aliases the admin registrar's `Router<'auth'>` signature requires; no controller or route-definition changes were needed. I then re-ran `bunx guren codegen`, which picked the new named route up into `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts`, and added `tests/AdminPostController.test.ts` covering both reported symptoms: a guest gets redirected to `/login`, and a signed-in user gets `200` with every post newest-first, each carrying its `author` `{ id, name }`.
